title: Nested context state sharing via meta versus obj
answers: What is the difference between Context.meta and Context.obj?
How do parent groups pass state down to child subcommands?
Why is Context.meta shared across nested contexts?
body:
In `src/click/core.py:Context`, `meta` is shared across all nested contexts in an execution tree, while `obj` is local to each context level.
- Rule: Cross-command extensions and utilities must store shared state in `ctx.meta` using dotted namespace keys (`src/click/core.py:Context.meta`). User state passed down command trees must use `ctx.obj` and be retrieved via `src/click/core.py:Context.find_object` or `src/click/core.py:Context.ensure_object`.
- Where enforced: `src/click/core.py:Context.__init__` sets `self._meta = parent.meta` if a parent context exists, whereas `self.obj` inherits from `parent.obj` by default but can be rebound independently per context.
- What breaks if skipped: Writing to `ctx.meta` with un-namespaced keys causes silent collisions between nested groups or plugins. Reassigning `ctx.obj` without `find_object` hides parent state from subcommands.
applies: Applies when threading state, configuration, or plugin metadata between parent Groups and child Commands.
says: Child subcommands cannot access configuration options set at the root command level.
Plugin data is overwriting user configuration when nesting multiple command levels together.
Pass global connection settings down to all nested subcommands automatically without re-prompting.
Subcommands fail because parent command state is lost during nested command dispatch.
Distinguish global extension settings from command-specific inputs across the command tree.
